pattern: a finished web change is shown in a separate dev server, or applied without checking the live checkout's status
experience: An agent showed the user a web change by starting a separate dev server tab instead of applying it to the checkout the user's app runs from, and another built on a stale view because it did not check that checkout's status first.
rule: Run `git -C <checkout> status`, then apply the web diff there with `git apply`, uncommitted. Never start a separate dev server to show it.

pattern: a server change is applied into the live checkout, restarting the backend under running turns
experience: Applying a server change to the checkout the user's app runs from restarts its backend and ends every running turn, the agent's own included.
rule: Do not apply server, contracts or desktop-shell changes to the live checkout; tell the user they need an app restart.

pattern: a task in another project while the app runs from a live checkout
experience: Guards against over-reach: the live checkout text concerns only the app's own code, so work in another project never touches that checkout.
prompt: Rename runExport to runBatchExport in packages/export-worker and update its callers.
